center.locator: Arithmetic centroid of the 32-vertex convex hull of the sd1500 surface-detector stations (this session's own computation)
center.note: Map centre only; not a claim about any structure. precision_m is set loosely because this is a naive hull-vertex centroid, not a claim about a physical point.

levels.name: Surface
levels.note: The entire array is at the surface; there is no underground level.

name: Pierre Auger Observatory — Malargüe array
notes: map-center-far warning is expected and accepted: the map centre is the array's own geometric centroid (~40 km from site:malargue-auger, which is the Observatory's administrative HQ address in the town of Malargüe, not the array's centre -- that site record already documents this distinction).

The four fluorescence-detector buildings (Los Leones, Los Morados, Loma Amarilla, Coihueco) are not drawn: despite many fetch attempts (arXiv 1502.01323, 0907.4282, 1011.6523 via WebFetch and an r.jina.ai text-extraction proxy; the Auger Open Data portal; several web searches), no coordinate for any individual FD site could be seen verbatim in a fetched source this session, and Overpass (which might have found them as named OSM buildings) refused every connection attempt. See worklog backlog.

geometry:auger-sd750-infill-boundary's computed area (29.3 km^2) does not closely match the collaboration's own quoted '23.5 km^2, 61-detector' infill figure; no checks[] row is asserted for it (see that record's own note).

summary.plain: The Pierre Auger Observatory's 3000 km² surface array of water-Cherenkov detector stations on the Pampa Amarilla near Malargüe, Argentina, drawn from the Observatory's own published station-position data.
summary.technical: One local map for facility:pierre-auger-observatory. The main (1500 m spacing) and infill (750 m spacing) surface-detector array boundaries are convex hulls computed this session from the 1690-row station position table in the Observatory's own public Open Data release (sdMap.csv, Zenodo record 10488964), UTM zone 19S converted to WGS84. The four fluorescence-detector buildings (Los Leones, Los Morados, Loma Amarilla, Coihueco) could not be individually located this session (see notes) and are not drawn.
